Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Dev: I checked the transfer logs from the last four runs. They landed between 2:21 and 2:34, so we have some room, but the March close export took almost twice as long to build. That one included the retro adjustments for the warehouse shift changes, not just the standard payroll fields.

Lina: For the normal file, we’re keeping the same column order and filename pattern. The bank reference and employee ID stay in the export, but the home address and personal email fields are still excluded. I’ll compare the header row against the February version before the file gets queued.

Mara: thanks. One thing I want to make clear is that the fallback only applies if Northstar SFTP is unavailable or the transfer hasn’t completed by 2:45. If the file is still building at that point, we should keep watching the run rather than send an unfinished export somewhere else.

Dev: yep, that matches the runbook. If the SFTP service is down, the backup route is the encrypted payroll portal, using the existing finance group access. We shouldn’t put the file in the general shared drive, even temporarily, because that folder has a much wider audience.

Lina: I can monitor the SFTP check from my side. If the transfer fails, I’ll post the exact error and the timestamp here, then pause before using the portal so we can confirm the file passed the row-count and total-pay checks. The backup route doesn’t skip those checks.

Jon: small note from Finance: they need one consolidated export, not separate files by department. Last month, the two-file version made it harder to reconcile the hourly staff adjustments, and the bank upload expects one file for this payroll group. Their usual import window closes at 3:30.

Mara: got it. If the regular export is too large for the portal limit, the fallback is to split it into the two payroll groups listed in the runbook, but only after Finance confirms they can accept both files. We shouldn’t assume that option is okay just because the upload accepts it.

Dev: I found the portal limit in the internal notes: 25 MB per upload. Thursday’s estimate is 18 to 21 MB, based on the current roster and the new tax codes, so it should fit. That estimate doesn’t include any late corrections submitted after the 1:45 cutoff.

Lina: The late-correction window is the main thing I’m watching. Payroll said, “we’ll flag anything received after cutoff before the export starts,” so I’ll wait for that message before I compare totals. If there’s a correction, the build may start later than 2:15.

Jon: Finance asked whether the portal sends an alert when the upload finishes. It does, but the alert only confirms receipt, not that the file imported successfully. They still need to reply in the channel after checking the total and the employee count in their system.

Mara: right, let’s keep those as separate checkpoints. A successful transfer means the file arrived; Finance’s import confirmation means they could read it. If they see a mismatch, they should hold the bank upload and send us the export name and the affected total, not a copy of the employee data.

Dev: for the monitoring handoff, I can cover 2:00 to 2:35, then Lina has the next window. If the job is still running at 2:35, I’ll leave the run ID and latest status in this thread so she doesn’t have to restart the check from scratch.

Lina: works for me. I’ll keep the payroll dashboard open and watch for a change from “building” to “ready.” I won’t download the file locally just to inspect it; the row count and control total are available in the restricted job view.

Mara: here’s the sequence I have in mind:
1. Confirm the correction cutoff message and start the regular build.
2. Check the header, row count, and control total in the restricted view.
3. Send through SFTP if it’s available; otherwise use the encrypted portal after the checks pass.
4. Ask Finance to confirm receipt and import separately.

Dev: that’s clear. One detail: the portal uses the same export name as the SFTP route, so we’ll need to say “portal” in the thread and include the transfer timestamp. That should help Finance distinguish the delivery method without changing the filename they use for reconciliation.

Jon: Finance also said they can stay online until 3:20, but not much later because their bank file review starts at 3:30. If we miss that window, they’ll hold the upload until the next business day rather than try to rush a manual import.

Mara: thanks for checking. Let’s not treat 3:20 as a reason to bypass validation. If the file arrives late or a check doesn’t match, post the status and we can coordinate with Finance on timing; nobody should send a partial export to meet the original window.

Lina: I’ll add the run ID, build start time, and delivery result to the payroll log after the handoff. For a portal delivery, I’ll record the portal receipt time too, but I won’t paste the file contents or any employee-level details into the log.

Dev: I’ll be around for questions during the first half of the window. The export job sometimes takes longer when the tax-code table refresh overlaps with the build, so if the status sits unchanged for ten minutes, I’ll check the job events before reporting it as stalled.

Jon: Finance has the same expectation on their end. Priya will watch for the file, and Omar is the backup if she has to leave for the bank review. They’ll post either the import confirmation or the reason they can’t complete it before the 3:20 handoff.

Mara: perfect, and please keep the thread updated even if the regular route works normally. I’m keeping Thursday’s notes with the payroll close checklist, including which delivery route was used and whether Finance confirmed the import.
